sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codification with Germanic and EU-law influences)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — freedom of establishment, free movement of capital and cross-border services
Luxembourg-United States Income Tax Treaty (signed 3 April 1996, as amended by Protocol of 20 May 2009)
Luxembourg-Germany Income and Capital Tax Treaty (signed 23 April 2012, in force 6 April 2013)
Luxembourg-China Double Taxation Convention and Protocol (signed 12 March 1994, in force 28 January 1996)
Luxembourg-Hong Kong SAR Income Tax Agreement (signed 6 November 2008, in force 13 July 2010)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network as applicable to Luxembourg
EU free trade and investment agreements applicable to Luxembourg (e.g., EU-Canada CETA, EU-Japan EPA, EU-Singapore FTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (implementing EU Directives (EU) 2015/849, (EU) 2018/843 and (EU) 2018/1673); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended to restrict general public access following CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 implementing the RBE; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Art. 710-1 et seq. for the SARL); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, and binding CSSF AML/CFT guidance; EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying funds transfers; FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 as transposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document for each shareholder and manager (natural person UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/identity authority or notary competent in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Contracting States) OR Consular Legalization by a Luxembourg embassy/consulate (non-Hague States)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each UBO and manager (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (where required by the Luxembourg notary or bank)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / excerpt of commercial register and UBO register excerpt where a shareholder is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or company registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of the corporate shareholder's articles of association and board resolution approving the establishment of the Luxembourg SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary of the corporate shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the initial share capital contribution (minimum EUR 12,000)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution where the shareholder maintains the funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization if requested by the receiving Luxembourg bank or notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, UBOs, managers and authorized signatories against (i) the Luxembourg PEP definition under the Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF Recommendation 12, (ii) EU Council consolidated sanctions lists including EU Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and (EU) 833/2014 as amended (Russia/Belarus and other EU autonomous regimes), (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iv) the OFAC SDN List and CAPTA List because USD-denominated payment rails (Stripe, Escrow_Pay) subject the merchant to US sanctions compliance, and (v) the FATF high-risk and monitored-jurisdiction lists; positive hits require enhanced due diligence, senior-management escalation and, where applicable, transaction blocks; for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced vintage-luxury resale platform, re-screening of UBOs and managers is required at least every 6 months and upon any ownership change, with continuous transaction monitoring and sanctions-list screening on all counterparties.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.screening_protocol_note: Access to the Luxembourg RBE is restricted to competent authorities (CSSF, financial intelligence unit, tax authorities, notaries, lawyers and regulated financial institutions) and, on a case-by-case basis, to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest in accordance with the amended Law of 13 January 2019; the UBO declaration must be filed within one month of incorporation via the Luxembourg Business Registers online platform.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online platform at www.lbr.lu (eJustice/LBR portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script; names in Luxembourgish, French, German, English or another language are accepted if rendered in Latin characters with a transliteration provided for non-Latin source names; the legal-form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear in the corporate name; the name must be distinctive, not misleading as to the company's activity, and must not create confusion with existing registered names, trademarks or protected trade names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (and translations such as Luxemburg/Lucemburgo) — requires prior ministerial authorization
Banque / Bank / Banking — requires CSSF-regulated banking license or ministerial derogation
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance / Reinsurance — requires regulated insurance-sector authorization
SICAV / SICAF / Fonds d'investissement / FCP / Investment Fund — requires CSSF fund-sector authorization
Bourse / Stock Exchange — requires financial-regulator authorization
État / State / National / Communal / Municipal / Governmental — implies public authority
Université / University / École / School / Academy — requires education-licensing authorization
Hôpital / Hospital / Clinique / Medical Center — requires health-sector licensing
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross / Red Crescent — protected emblems under Geneva Conventions legislation
SA / S.A. / Société Anonyme — may only be used by public limited companies, not by an SARL
SARL / S.à r.l. — may only be used if the entity is actually incorporated as a SARL
Rolex, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Cartier and other famous luxury trademarks — rejected on prior-rights and anti-counterfeiting grounds for the vintage luxury resale scope
Luxury / Vintage / Resale / Brocante — permitted only if consistent with the actual activity and not misleading
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name clearance is requested electronically through the LBR portal, which blocks the proposed name for a 5-week (35-day) validity window pending submission of the notarized incorporation deed; if the requested name is refused by the RCS registrar on grounds of confusion, misleading character, prohibited token or insufficient distinctiveness, the applicant may either (i) modify the name and immediately file a new reservation request through the LBR portal without charge, or (ii) lodge a formal appeal ('recours en réformation') against the registrar's refusal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within 15 days of the notification of refusal, in accordance with the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and the New Code of Civil Procedure; the appeal must be brought by a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour, the court may substitute its own decision and order registration, and a further appeal lies to the Cour d'appel; where the incorporation is not completed before the 35-day expiry, the name may be reserved again by filing a new blocking request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially acceptable: a pure virtual office consisting of mail-forwarding only is not permissible as the statutory seat of a Luxembourg SARL, because the company must maintain a real registered office in Luxembourg and produce genuine economic substance under the Law of 27 December 2021 implementing the EU ATAD anti-abuse rules; however, the use of a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent's address ('domiciliation légale') is expressly permitted and is market-standard for e-commerce operating companies, provided that day-to-day management, board decisions, accounting records, bank accounts and AML/CFT compliance functions are effectively directed and managed from Luxembourg; for the vintage luxury resale business using Stripe and Escrow_Pay, a physical commercial store is not required, but the SARL must retain Luxembourg substance proportionate to its turnover and headcount.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High: quantified 30–40% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection or substance review by the RCS/RBE authority, the CSSF (AML supervision delegated for non-financial sector operators), or the Luxembourg direct tax administration within the first 24 months of operation for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced online luxury-resale SARL; the first-year probability is approximately 20% in the absence of adverse risk signals, but increases materially upon VAT registration, opening of a Luxembourg bank account, high-value cross-border transactions, or merchant onboarding of high-risk payment rails.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.substance_obligation_note: The SARL must keep in Luxembourg its registered office, statutory books, accounting records, minutes of shareholders' and managers' decisions, and a Luxembourg bank account; the registered office must be indicated in the articles of association and in the RCS; any change of registered office requires amendment of the articles by notarial deed and RCS filing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and blocking request via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: free of charge for the electronic name pre-check and 35-day blocking

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarization of the SARL articles of association (statuts) in notarial authentic form
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff plus drafting fees; prevailing market benchmark EUR 1,200–1,600 plus VAT and disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the incorporation deed with the RCS and issuance of the RCS extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee of approximately EUR 75–85 per filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in the RESA official electronic gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff of approximately EUR 60 per notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner declaration filing in the RBE (register of beneficial owners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee of approximately EUR 30; frequently waived when filed electronically together with the initial RCS registration within the incorporation window

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of passport copies, address proofs and corporate UBO documents of foreign shareholders and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each Hague Convention contracting state or Luxembourg embassy/consulate for non-Hague-state documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark USD 100–250 depending on document count and country of origin; Luxembourg-issued apostilles are generally free of charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT due diligence, UBO piercing analysis, PEP/OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening and pre-incorporation legal clearance opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (member of the Luxembourg Bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee EUR 2,000–3,500, or hourly rate EUR 350–450 per attorney

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation agreement with a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (first 12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark EUR 2,400–3,000 per annum plus VAT and resident-agent due-diligence fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial attestation of payment of the minimum share capital (EUR 12,000) and bank blocking certificate for the capital deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary and Luxembourg credit institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial certificate fee of EUR 80–150 plus the bank's capital-confirmation charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Merchant onboarding and AML/merchant-risk compliance advisory for Stripe and Escrow_Pay payment rails
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External payments-compliance counsel and advisory boutique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee of EUR 900–1,400 for payment-rail compliance review, AML onboarding and merchant-risk assessment

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 to 710-25 for the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 July 2017 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 13c, rue de Bitbourg, L-1273 Luxembourg-Hamm; online portal: e-justice.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of association (Statuts) constituting the SARL, filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL requires a minimum issued share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up before incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account in the name of the company-in-formation with a Luxembourg credit institution and may be released only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions must be evaluated by a statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) with a full valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the first board of managers of the SARL, that: (1) the incorporation deed and articles of association, as executed and filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers, are hereby ratified; (2) the issue and subscription of the Company's EUR 12,000 ordinary share capital, fully paid up into a blocked Luxembourg bank account, are approved; (3) the registered office is fixed at [insert address] in Luxembourg; (4) [Name] and [Name] are appointed managers, each authorized to act jointly or severally; (5) banking, accounting, filing and online platform arrangements are authorized; (6) the managers are empowered to complete all post-formation formalities. This resolution is effective as of today.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and reservation with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online via e-justice.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request for the proposed corporate name, ensuring it complies with Luxembourg legal principles of public order and does not conflict with an existing registered name or trademark. Provide the proposed legal form 'SARL' and the corporate purpose in sufficiently specific terms for the resale of vintage luxury goods.
required_dossiers: Extract of the desired legal form and corporate purpose
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an administrative objection with the RCS, submit alternative proposed names, or seek a prior written opinion from the RCS on a revised name before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the blocked capital account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or bank selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company-in-formation and deposit the full EUR 12,000 cash contribution. Obtain a capital certificate (certificat de dépôt de fonds) or blocked-funds confirmation from the bank, which will be released only upon presentation of the RCS registration extract.
required_dossiers: Description of the cash contribution source for anti-money-laundering KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the deposit or KYC documentation, provide enhanced beneficial-ownership statements and source-of-funds evidence; if the bank refuses, select an alternative Luxembourg-regulated credit institution and restart the block account procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the incorporation deed before a Luxembourg notary. The notary will verify the legality of the articles, the identity and legal capacity of all shareholders, the compliance of the capital deposit, and the availability of the corporate name. The deed must expressly state the corporate purpose, the registered office address, the share capital, the number of shares, and the appointment of managers.
required_dossiers: Bank capital certificate or blocked-funds confirmation
Identity documents of shareholders and managers
Written consent of the proposed managers
Draft articles of association reviewed by Luxembourg counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in the deed or articles, amend the deed promptly and hold a new notarial execution; any delay in notarization does not invalidate the capital block and may be cured by issuing an amended deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), e-justice.lu portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial incorporation deed and supporting statements electronically with the RCS. Pay the statutory registration fee and await the legal review. The RCS will verify the legality of the deed, the registered office, the subscribed capital, and the appointment of managers before issuing the registration extract.
required_dossiers: Identity documents and signatures of managers
Declaration of non-bankruptcy and no professional disqualification of managers
Power of attorney to the filing agent if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a formal observation or request for correction, cure the irregularity within the given deadline, typically by filing an amending deed or supplemental declaration. If the registration is refused, appeal to the Luxembourg district court within the statutory time limit or resubmit after rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal publication in the RESA electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Publication Department, Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the registry automatically publishes the required legal particulars in the RESA. Confirm publication and download the publication notice, which evidences completion of incorporation formalities against third parties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, file a written correction request with LBR/RCS; if a third party challenges the publication, rely on the RCS registration date and apply to the court for a corrective order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation registrations: VAT, social security, and establishment authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy for establishment authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL for Luxembourg VAT under national VAT number, register shareholders/managers with the CCSS for social security, and obtain the general establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) required to operate the online resale business. Complete these filings immediately after RCS registration to ensure legal operation.
required_dossiers: Excerpt of the criminal record (casier judiciaire) of managers
Proof of professional competence or business plan for the establishment authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT or CCSS returns a query, provide additional documentation and pay any administrative late fees promptly. If the establishment authorization is refused or delayed, submit a new application with a full business plan and, if necessary, seek review by the Minister of the Economy or before the administrative tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie), Directorate-General for Industry and Commerce; municipal authority competent for the registered office premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Establishment Authorization (Autorisation d'établissement) for commercial distribution and online retail activities; where physical storage is used, a municipal operating permit for commercial premises may also apply

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Agency – Administration de l'environnement (National Administration for the Environment), Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report; an EIA registration notice is required only if the proposed warehouse or logistics facility exceeds the screening thresholds under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment. For ordinary online retail warehousing below such thresholds, registration with the water and waste authority is sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are generated by the resale activity. Packaging waste from returned or unsold luxury goods must comply with the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 1997, as amended), including sorting and recovery obligations. Waste electrical or electronic equipment, if any, is governed by the EU WEEE Directive implemented in Luxembourg. Discharge of any cleaning or firefighting waters must respect municipal sewer regulations and the general duty of care under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for any office, showroom, or warehouse must be obtained from the municipal fire prevention authority (Inspection du service d'incendie et de secours) and the Commune's building inspectorate, including a structural load certification for storage areas. Occupational clearance from the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du travail et des mines, ITM) is required to confirm ergonomic workstations, safe access, emergency exits, and compliance with the Labour Code for employees. For a purely online consignment business without physical handling of goods, only office-related occupational safety certificates and a fire evacuation plan are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg VAT and Registration Administration; online portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities established outside Luxembourg must register for VAT directly via MyGuichet or, if established outside the EU, appoint a tax representative domiciled in Luxembourg. The application requires submission of the RCSL extract (for EU entities), power of attorney, and proof of economic activity. The Luxembourg VAT identification number is assigned in the format 'LU' followed by 8 digits, typically within 10 to 15 business days after submission.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg. A SARL is inherently opaque and subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax. Optional VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') is available to related taxable persons. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply and may disallow deductions or reclassify payments; no elective hybrid regime is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic small-business exemption threshold: EUR 35,000 annual turnover. Intra-EU distance sales threshold: EUR 10,000 (Union-wide). Non-established foreign sellers have mandatory registration with no turnover threshold for Luxembourg VAT purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control system. Electronic invoicing is mandatory only for invoices issued to central government entities using PEPPOL BIS / EN 16931 format. B2B e-invoicing requires customer consent. No digital stamping or government pre-clearance is required; invoices must preserve authenticity, integrity, and legibility.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier, the buyer, or a third party acting on behalf of either qualify for the 0% export VAT rate if the export is completed within 3 months of supply. The seller must hold documentary proof of export. Offshore B2B services and services directly related to export goods may also be zero-rated. For vintage luxury resale, the second-hand goods margin scheme cannot be combined with zero-rating on the same transaction; if margin scheme is applied, the supply remains taxable in the EU unless an explicit export waiver is exercised.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / electronic customs declaration through EU CTAS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Bank Transfer Proof
Transport Evidence (CMR waybill, carrier tracking report, or courier proof of delivery)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT authority may audit export evidence for up to 5 years. Missing or fraudulent export substantiation triggers retrospective VAT assessment at 17%, late interest, and administrative fines up to 100% of the tax evaded. Criminal prosecution for serious VAT fraud and export zero-rating abuse can impose fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of directors. Reclaimed input VAT associated with disallowed zero-rated exports is clawed back with penalty surcharges; due diligence on transport documents and payment traceability is mandatory.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and exchange-control oversight; foreign exchange policy is harmonized at EU level through Economic and Monetary Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full and unrestricted capital and current account convertibility for euro-based and foreign-currency transactions under EU Treaty provisions (Art. 63 TFEU) and the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2002 on the payments system. There are no exchange-control barriers to inbound equity injections, profit distributions, dividend remittances, or loan repayments, provided the underlying documentation satisfies standard corporate law, tax compliance, and AML/CFT due diligence. The SARL is subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax, and net wealth tax, but foreign exchange conversion is not taxed. Profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders is permitted assimilated to dividend distribution, subject to withholding tax (15% standard, reduced to 0% under a properly applied EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable DTT if 10% participation holding is maintained for 12 months). No Central Bank pre-approval is required for transfers exceeding any threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligations or mandatory conversion ratios in Luxembourg or within the Eurozone. Export receipts from cross-border vintage luxury resale, whether denominated in EUR, USD, GBP, or other currencies, may be retained in foreign-currency accounts at Luxembourg credit institutions or in EU-licensed payment accounts. No BCL declaration is required for trade-related current account transactions, though amounts above EUR 15,000 must be reported by the credit institution to the CSSF/BCL as part of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) transaction-monitoring protocols. For statistical balance-of-payments reporting, the BCL requires banks to use standardized purpose codes (e.g., service codes for e-commerce intermediation), but no surrender ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Separate EUR and Foreign-Currency Accounts
Capital Escrow Account / Cross-Border Operational Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Clearing Facility
Operational Account and FX Hedging Envelope

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability for operational collections and settlement through EU passporting under PSD2, e.g., Stripe Treasury, Adyen, or a Luxembourg-licensed EMI such as Licks or ZEN, for daily e-commerce flows in EUR, USD, and GBP. These platforms accelerate merchant onboarding for resale marketplaces and offer API-based payment orchestration. However, EMIs cannot serve as a substitute for a regulated credit institution for capital escrow, inward equity injections, commercial letters of credit, or FX hedging line establishment, because the SARL must maintain segregated client funds in a commercial bank for fiduciary and audit defensibility. Legal constraint: EMIs do not have CDD authority in all third-country jurisdictions; they cannot issue documentary credits (LC) and they are not counterparties under ISDA/EMIR for non-deliverable forwards. The SARL should therefore maintain one primary tier-1 bank account for capital and treasury operations and one EMI account as a collection conduit subject to daily zero-balance sweeps.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a universal statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in branch; remote account opening is permitted if a videoconference with a compliance officer is completed and identity verification is conducted via qualified electronic signature or eIDAS. However, most tier-1 banks, when the beneficial owner and director are not EU residents, require at least one in-person interview at the Luxembourg branch for the managing director (gérant) or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact with notarized power of attorney. The Corporate as Client questionnaire must be supplemented with authenticated passports, proof of residential address, original notarized articles of association, and the Luxembourg trade register (RCS) extract. If a non-EU parent exists, a certified copy of the ultimate beneficial ownership register (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) and a signed compliance undertaking are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic exposure of beneficial owners or counterparties purchasing luxury goods from sanctioned-risk corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adverse-media and sanctions screening results, risk-mitigation narrative explaining that all buyers and sellers are screened against EU/UN/OFAC lists using an automated screening tool, a documented enhanced due diligence (EDD) questionnaire, and proof that all transactions remain in the secondhand luxury category without arms or dual-use exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity in source-of-wealth for the SARL's capital injection and subsequent cross-border inbound transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital subscription deed showing the ultimate financing source, bank statements of the contributing shareholder for the last 12 months evidencing lawful accumulation of funds, audited or certified accounting statements of the parent if corporate shareholder, and a sworn declaration on source of wealth in accordance with CSSF Regulation 12-02.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction-velocity pattern characteristic of digital resale platforms (frequent high-volume, low-value cross-border inbound/outbound payments).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed operating model memorandum demonstrating legitimate e-commerce consignment activity, an inventory ledger matching goods purchase and sale flows, a breached escrow arrangement with a licensed payment processor, and contractual agreements with suppliers and buyers specifying payment rails, to justify ticket-size distributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) qualified as politically exposed person (PEP) or having a high net worth requiring enhanced scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete PEP declaration and status justification, a prominent public-position analysis showing no corruption or conviction risk, at least three independent reference letters from regulated financial or legal institutions, and a documented source-of-funds trail for any transaction involving the PEP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank's concern over regulatory classification of luxury resale as mixed 'e-commerce' vs 'auction house' triggering anti-money laundering thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion by a Luxembourg counsel confirming that the activity falls under ISIC 4791 and is not subject to the Luxembourg Auctioneers Law of 24 July 2021 (no statutory licensing), and an AML/CFT operational memorandum describing transaction monitoring thresholds, suspicious-transaction reporting procedures to the CRF (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers), record-keeping retention for five years, and the appointment of a compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound capital contributions from the ultimate shareholder through the primary tier-1 Luxembourg bank using SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) in EUR if the contributor is within an EEA jurisdiction, or SWIFT MT103 (CBPR+) with essential fields charged to the beneficiary's cash account. The wire instruction must include purpose code 'PCAP' (Paid-in Capital) or 'EQUI' (Equity) in the SWIFT purpose field and reference the notarized capital subscription deed and the RCS registration number of the SARL. Beneficiary account must be identified as the capital escrow/operational account in the name of LU_SARL, and the bank requires the submission of the notarized deed, an updated RCS extract, and certification of no capital laundering. Verification of the originator's identity and of the absence of sanctioned jurisdictions is performed; the bank shall block or request enhanced checks if the originator's account is in a non-cooperative jurisdiction per FATF.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to EU-based suppliers of vintage luxury items, use the SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated settlement. For non-EEA suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 with value date t+1, including standard remittance details of the purchase invoice, and retain all TARIC/Intrastat declarations where applicable. For high-value consignment collections (above EUR 100,000), the bank may open a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) as an irrevocable LC with a trusted issuing bank, particularly for physical handover consignment gorunds in Geneva, Dubai, or Miami; in that case, documents must include the bill of lading, securely vaulted condition reports, certificates of authenticity (e.g., third-party authentication, immutability checks), and insurance coverage. Payment aggregation through Stripe or Escrow Pay is permissible for the front-end collection layer, subject to daily zero-balancing sweeps to the tier-1 bank account, and for trade settlements to the buyer/seller marketplace, use the processor's local payout rails or SWIFT MT103 for cross-border seller payouts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot EUR/USD and EUR/GBP conversions cleared on T+2 for operating receipts and inventory replenishment
Forward FX contracts (maturity 1, 3, 6, and 12 months) with the tier-1 bank covering committed purchase settlement in USD and GBP, with automatic rollover if market orders cancelled
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in restricted currencies (e.g., CNY or INR) where physical delivery is impossible in the offshore market, with a documented underlying trade exposure
Cross-currency swaps for multi-year lease agreements or substantial capital expenditure commitments in a non-EUR currency, subject to board approval and treasury policy limits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Accounts (financial statements) filing to RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers summons by the Public Prosecutor, publication of the conviction, administrative and criminal fines ranging from EUR 200 up to EUR 25,000, and potential judicial dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following the annual anniversary of the initial RBE registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or materially incorrect UBO data constitutes a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment (6 months to 5 years) and/or fines up to EUR 250,000 for individuals and up to EUR 750,000 for legal entities; daily administrative penalties may also be imposed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for SARLs exceeding two of three criteria: balance sheet total > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average workforce > 50 employees. Public interest entities and undertakings exceeding these thresholds must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Commercial Code, Title II) with IFRS permitted for statutory reporting under certain conditions; consolidated accounts under IFRS if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the RBE law, SARLs must confirm the accuracy of beneficial-owner data annually within one month of the registration anniversary. Any change in shareholding or voting control must be reported within 30 days of the change; the annual confirmation reflects all ownership transfers and control adjustments for the preceding 12 months.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% base corporate income tax (plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax; maximum combined headline incidence in Luxembourg City is 24.94%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg SARL may benefit from the 80% IP-box exemption on qualifying intellectual property income, producing a reduced effective rate of about 4.98%; the participation exemption fully exempts qualifying dividends and capital gains from CIT; additional incentives include the super-deduction for R&D and investment tax credits; advance tax agreements (ATAs) are available for substantive structures.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited for losses incurred from tax year 2017 onwards; losses from earlier years remain subject to the former 10-year carryforward regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 720/730 corporate income tax return (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed through the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) electronic portal MyTaxFile / RTS system via Guichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly CIT prepayments are separately remitted during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due no later than 31 December of the following calendar year; for non-calendar year-ends, the return is due within twelve months of the fiscal year-end. Extensions are available on reasoned request before the filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal form, registered office, RCS registration number, LEI, fiscal year start and end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg SARL's local establishment data; a foreign manager or shareholder must identify its overseas address and tax residence in the annexes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting income: net profit before tax as per Luxembourg GAAP / financial statements, adjusted for non-deductible expenses and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a French or English reconciliation from the statutory accounts; do not net out foreign withholding taxes or remittances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption disclosures: qualifying shareholding percentage, cost threshold, and 12-month holding condition for dividend and capital gains exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide supporting shareholder registers and subscription agreements to evidence the holding period for non-resident corporate shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IP-box deduction: computation of qualifying intangible property income and the 80% exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Luxembourg-resident entities with local economic substance and qualifying IP rights may elect; foreign licensors cannot directly claim this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset: amount of previously assessed taxable losses applied against current-year profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss carryforward is available to the same legal taxpayer only; a change in ownership or business purpose can invalidate the continuity requirement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base: total taxable income after all adjustments, deductions, and netting of prior losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must not allocate Luxembourg taxable income offshore merely because management decisions are made abroad; locus of effective management and substance remain decisive.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: CIT at 17%, solidarity surcharge of 7% on CIT, municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and alternative minimum corporate income tax where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the municipal multiplier for the commune of the registered office; city-centre and rural communes differ.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes, prepayments, and tax credits: advance CIT payments, dividend WHT already suffered, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign tax credit calculations on a treaty basis and do not claim UK/US foreign taxes without a Luxembourg ACD credit form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions and transfer pricing declaration: intercompany sales, purchases, management fees, financing, and arm's-length methodology.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with non-resident related parties even if below EUR 1 million aggregate; hidden profit distributions are assessed at the shareholder level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax cross-reference and annual net wealth tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL remains subject to net wealth tax even if all shareholders are non-resident; minimum net wealth tax rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director certification and signature: board approval of the tax return and assumption of responsibility.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The in-Luxembourg director or statutory representative must sign; a power of attorney from the foreign sole shareholder is insufficient unless recorded with the ACD.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers coercive reminders and tax ex officio assessment; late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month; a 10% late-payment penalty applies after two months; intentional under-declaration or concealment can attract penalties of 20% to 80% of the evaded tax and criminal proceedings under Luxembourg general tax law (AO) and the Criminal Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on distributions to non-resident shareholders; domestic inter-corporate dividends qualifying for participation exemption are exempt when the recipient holds at least 10% of the payer or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1,200,000 and satisfies the 12-month holding condition; reduced rates or 0% apply under tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduction, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a certificate of residence from its own tax authority, submit it to the Luxembourg ACD, complete the ACD relief request form (RTS / form 105 for dividends), and, if relief is not granted at source, apply for a refund within the statutory limitation period; for EU parent companies, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive is implemented through the participation exemption and formal WHT exemption procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest; arm's-length interest and royalty payments to non-residents are generally free of source tax. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive and Luxembourg domestic law confirm a 0% rate; this also applies to payments made to related EU companies. Participating loan interest and anti-abuse exceptions may apply in artificial arrangements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg does not impose a fixed local-file threshold in domestic legislation; the ACD requires transfer-pricing documentation to be supplied when related-party transactions are material, commonly where the aggregate value exceeds EUR 1,000,000. Mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting applies to MNC groups with annual consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000, in which case the Luxembourg entity must file its CbCR declaration through the ACD portal.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations similar to other financial-centre statutes, but substance is enforced through the Luxembourg GAAR (abuse of law doctrine), ATAD provisions, and LIR anti-deferral rules. A SARL must demonstrate commercial substance through a registered office, local management, employee/decision-maker capacity, bank accounts, accounting and corporate records maintained in Luxembourg, and annual board or shareholder meetings. Absent substance, tax benefits, treaty access, and participation-exemption treatment can be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting online luxury-resale turnover from the annual CIT return, maintaining dual or shadow books, treating personal vintage acquisitions as business expenses, inflating intercompany management fees to shift profits to a zero-tax jurisdiction, or deliberately under-reporting escrow settlement amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable income plus default interest of 0.6% per month; late-payment penalty of 10%; civil penalties of 20% to 80% of the evaded tax for intentional fault; criminal prosecution can lead to fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; surrender of unlawfully obtained tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for taxes not withheld or deliberately evaded if they sign false returns or tolerate shadow accounting; personal assets can be seized, travel bans imposed, and directors can be imprisoned where their involvement is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell / letterbox company and abusive structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a registered office in Luxembourg with no staff, no premises, no local bank account, no local board meeting minutes, with all commercial decisions on pricing, supply, escrow, and payment routing taken by a foreign beneficial owner; using a Luxembourg SARL solely to obtain treaty benefits or VAT advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the entity for tax purposes under the Luxembourg anti-abuse doctrine; denial of tax residence certificate, participation exemption, treaty relief, and VAT registration; imposition of tax at the level of the actual beneficial owner; fines and civil penalties for failure to demonstrate economic substance in audit proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sham entity can be held personally liable to the tax administration for taxes that should have been borne by the entity, repay artificial distributions, suffer disqualification as directors, be subject to travel restrictions, and face criminal sanctions where the sham was used to facilitate fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, unlicensed escrow, and payment-rail misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a vintage-luxury resale platform without appointing a Luxembourg AML compliance officer or without the required AML/CFT internal procedures; holding or settling buyer/seller client funds through escrow or Stripe without proper money-transmitter or payment-institution authorisation; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the Luxembourg FIU; proceeding with deluxe consignment transactions when the beneficial owner or counterparty appears on sanctioned lists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 under Luxembourg AML/CFT laws; withdrawal of the payment service provider's licence or termination of bank/PSP relationships; freezing of escrow wallets and Stripe reserves; criminal money-laundering penalties up to ten years' imprisonment; prohibition from conducting the resale activity; potential seizure of online business property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil restitution for client funds lost or misused, joint liability for fines if they knowingly allowed the unlicensed activity, personal criminal liability for AML breaches, asset freezing orders, foreign travel bans, and imprisonment where escrow funds were knowingly used to conceal illicit wealth.
